question.text: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> moving with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> strikes the bob of a pendulum at rest. The mass of the bob is also <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math>. If the collision is perfectly inelastic, the height to which the bob will rise is given by <!-- MathType@Translator@5@5@MathML2 (namespace attr).tdl@MathML 2.0 (namespace attr)@ --> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>, <!-- MathType@End@5@5@ --> then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is<!-- MathType@End@5@5@ -->

solution.text:
Because the collision is perfectly inelastic, the two blocks stick together. By conservation of linear momentum,

     2mV=mv  or V=v2

By conservation of energy,

    2mgh=12×2mV2  or h=v28·g

⇒x=8
